spec.goal: Add the repository's only CI workflow, .github/workflows/ci.yml, so that every push to any branch and every pull_request runs both committed test suites unattended on a fresh checkout. One GitHub Actions job on ubuntu-latest checks out the repo (actions/checkout pinned to a major version tag), sets up Node 20 (actions/setup-node pinned to a major version tag, matching the root package.json engines field ">=20"), installs dependencies with `npm ci` in the repository root and again in toy/ (both have a committed lockfileVersion-3 package-lock.json and neither node_modules directory is tracked — .gitignore line 1 is `node_modules/`), then runs the root suite (`npm test` → `node --test "substrate/test/*.test.js"`) and the toy suite (`npm test` in toy/ → `NODE_ENV=test node --test "test/*.test.js"`) as two separately named steps, so a reader of the Actions log can tell from the step name alone which suite failed. Either failing suite fails the job. This closes HANDOFF.md C4: today every green number in HANDOFF.md §5 came from a human running the suites by hand. Verification lands as a new node:test file under substrate/test/ that reads the workflow file as text and asserts its structure; the repository has no YAML parser among its dependencies (root deps are ajv and ajv-formats only) and adding one is out of scope, so assertions are regex/line-shape assertions in the style of substrate/test/AC-17-implementer-boundary-doc.test.js.

acceptance.given: a clone of the repository at the merge commit for this work item
acceptance.then: exactly one workflow file exists, at .github/workflows/ci.yml, it is non-empty, it contains no tab characters, and it has the three top-level keys `name:`, the trigger key (`on:`, `"on":` or `'on':`), and `jobs:` each at column 0

it declares both `push` and `pull_request`, and the `push` trigger carries no branch allowlist that would exclude a branch (either no `branches:` key under push, or `branches:` whose only entry is the `'**'` wildcard), so a push to a branch such as claude/company-graph-carry-list-e2z510 triggers a run

the only actions referenced are actions/checkout and actions/setup-node, and each is pinned to a major version tag matching `@v[0-9]+` exactly (no `@main`, `@master`, no branch or floating ref, no bare action name)
it sets `node-version` to 20 (as `20`, `'20'` or `"20"`, not a range, not a `node-version-file`), matching the `engines.node` value ">=20" in ./package.json

acceptance.when: the `run:` commands are read in file order
acceptance.then: a step runs `npm ci` against the repository root (a `run: npm ci` with no `working-directory:` other than `.`), and it appears before the step that runs the root suite

acceptance.when: the `run:` commands are read in file order
acceptance.then: a step runs `npm ci` against toy/ — either `run: cd toy && npm ci` or `run: npm ci` with `working-directory: toy` — and it appears before the step that runs the toy suite

acceptance.when: the step that runs the root suite is read
acceptance.then: it is its own step with its own `name:` that identifies it as the root/substrate suite, and its `run:` invokes the package script unmodified (`npm test`, optionally `npm test --`, with no `working-directory:` other than `.`) rather than re-spelling `node --test` or any path glob

acceptance.when: the step that runs the toy suite is read
acceptance.then: it is a separate step from AC-7 with its own distinct `name:` that identifies it as the toy suite, and its `run:` invokes the toy package script unmodified — `cd toy && npm test`, or `npm test` with `working-directory: toy` — rather than re-spelling `node --test`, `NODE_ENV=test` or any path glob
the root-suite command and the toy-suite command appear in two different steps (they are not two lines of one multi-line `run:` block), so an Actions log attributes a failure to a named step

acceptance.when: the two suite steps and the two install steps are read
acceptance.then: none of them carries `continue-on-error: true`, and none of their `run:` bodies contains a failure-swallowing construct (`|| true`, `|| :`, `|| exit 0`, `set +e`), so a non-zero exit from either suite fails the job
there is exactly one job, it declares `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, and the file contains no `strategy:` or `matrix:` key

acceptance.when: the whole file is searched for out-of-scope machinery
acceptance.then: it contains no `cache:` or `cache-dependency-path:` key, no lint/coverage invocation (`npm run lint`, `eslint`, `--coverage`, `c8`, `nyc`), no deploy/publish/release step (`npm publish`, `actions/upload-artifact`, `softprops/action-gh-release`, `gh release`), and no `secrets.` reference

acceptance.when: it is searched for hardcoded expectations about suite size
acceptance.then: it asserts no specific passing-test count anywhere — the counts quoted in the work item intent are already stale (the root suite is 114 passing today, not 105; the toy suite is 60), and a CI file that greps for a number would go red the next time a test is added

acceptance.when: the paths the workflow installs against are checked
acceptance.then: ./package-lock.json and ./toy/package-lock.json are both tracked by git (so `npm ci` can succeed in both locations) and neither ./node_modules nor ./toy/node_modules is tracked, confirming the install steps are load-bearing rather than decorative

acceptance.given: a fresh checkout with no node_modules in either location
acceptance.when: the workflow's `run:` commands are executed in file order in their declared working directories
acceptance.then: both installs succeed and both suites exit 0 — the root suite reporting `# fail 0` and the toy suite reporting `# fail 0` — which is the behavior this workflow exists to automate

out_of_scope: Linting of any kind — no eslint, prettier, markdownlint, or actionlint step, and no lint config file.
Coverage reporting or thresholds (c8, nyc, --experimental-test-coverage) and any coverage upload.
Matrix builds: no `strategy:`/`matrix:` key, no second Node version, no second OS, no non-ubuntu-latest or self-hosted runner.
Dependency caching: no `cache: npm` on setup-node, no `cache-dependency-path:`, no actions/cache step.
Deployment, publishing, and release automation of every kind, including artifact upload and GitHub Releases.
Any second workflow file — this item adds .github/workflows/ci.yml and nothing else under .github/ (no dependabot.yml, no CODEOWNERS, no PR or issue templates).
Modifying ./package.json or ./toy/package.json — the `test` scripts and the `engines` field are consumed as they are, not edited.

Adding, removing, or upgrading any npm dependency, including a YAML parser for the verification test; the verification test asserts on the file as text, in the style of substrate/test/AC-17-implementer-boundary-doc.test.js.
Changing any existing test, fixture, or helper under ./substrate/test/ or ./toy/test/, and changing any source under ./substrate/ or ./toy/src/.
Making the two suites pass — both are green today (root 114 passing, toy 60 passing); this item automates running them, and fixing a red suite is a separate work item.
Asserting or updating specific passing-test counts anywhere, in the workflow or in the docs.
Repository settings that live outside the tree: branch protection, required status checks, Actions permissions, environments, and secrets.
Updating HANDOFF.md (§5 phase status, or C4 in §6) or any other markdown to record that CI now exists.
Running or wiring any workflow under .claude/workflows/ into CI — those are Claude Code workflow scripts, not CI jobs, and CI never invokes an agent.
Anything about wi-c5-gate-delivery, gate notification, or /create-project §6's CI-standup step, even though C4 names that as the reason venture 0 never got CI.
risk_reasons: Purely additive: creates two new files (.github/workflows/ci.yml and substrate/test/ci-workflow.test.js) without modifying any existing code
No stored data shape changes: workflow configuration and test code do not alter contracts or schemas
No auth, secrets, payments, or infrastructure impact: uses only pinned public GitHub Actions without credential injection
No runtime code changes: substrate CLIs, workflow scripts, and application logic remain untouched
Fully reversible: files can be deleted without side effects or deployed state consequences
No external client impact: venture 0 is self-contained with no downstream consumers
No contract breakage: all existing agents, workflows, and service contracts remain valid
Explicit out-of-scope boundary prevents scope creep and unintended changes

tasks.description: Implement the GitHub Actions CI workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs both test suites on every push and pull request, and create the verification test file at substrate/test/ci-workflow.test.js to validate the workflow structure and execution behavior against all acceptance criteria.
